name: Gradient-weighted L2 Loss
definition: A loss function that approximates the gradient of a tonemapped loss (e.g., L2 on tonemapped values) by weighting the standard L2 residual by the derivative of the tone curve, allowing stable training with noisy raw data without diverging.
summary: Gradient-weighted L2 Loss stabilizes training on noisy HDR images by weighting L2 residuals with the tone curve derivative, suppressing gradients in bright regions to prevent divergence.
